title: Hajar in the valley
hookLine: Ibrahim leaves Hajar and baby Isma'il in a dry valley, and she asks: did Allah command this? then we will not be lost
carry: then we will not be lost

lines: A VALLEY WITH NOTHING IN IT.
cards: A valley with nothing in it. No trees, no well, no town. Rock on both sides, heat coming up off the ground.

A man walks in with a woman and a baby, sets down a leather bag of dates and a skin of water, and turns to go. She gets up and follows him. Ibrahim, are you leaving us here, in a valley with no people and nothing in it?
He doesn't answer. She asks again. He keeps walking, and he doesn't look back.
What she asks next is short, and it isn't an accusation.

teach.b: This story isn't told in the Qur'an itself. It comes from a long hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated from Ibn Abbas. Hajar is the mother of Ibrahim's son Isma'il; Jews and Christians know her as Hagar, from Genesis.
She follows Ibrahim, asking, and he won't answer. So she changes the question.
Did Allah command you to do this? He says yes.

teach.h: HE WILL NOT LET US BE LOST.
teach.b: And she says, in effect: then He will not let us be lost. And she walks back to her baby. She didn't stop asking.

She found the one question that mattered, got her answer, and let it hold her. That's not the same as feeling fine. The dates and water are about to run out, and tomorrow we'll see what that costs her.

But her trust is the ground she stands on while she runs. Then the hadith gives us Ibrahim's side. When he reached a place where they couldn't see him, he turned toward the valley, raised his hands and prayed.

teach.h: A PRAYER FROM OUT OF SIGHT.
teach.b: That prayer is in the Qur'an, in Surah Ibrahim: our Lord, I have settled some of my children in a valley without crops, near Your sacred House, so that they may establish prayer.
So make the hearts of people incline toward them, and provide them with fruits, that they may give thanks. He didn't look back at them.
But out of sight, he looked back at the valley, and asked for everything they'd need. That empty valley is Mecca. Pilgrims now walk where she stood.

how: Muslims remember Hajar at Mecca, where the valley she was left in became the city around the Ka'ba; her trust is often retold in sermons on tawakkul, reliance on Allah.

o: a prophet's daughter who led her people
Isma'il's mother, left in the valley with him
Ibrahim's sister, who traveled with him

games.q: who did what in the story — tap the pairs.
p: walked away and didn't look back
dates, and a skin of water
Ibrahim raised his hands and prayed

s: the Qur'an tells the whole story of Hajar in the valley
the story comes from a hadith in Bukhari. the Qur'an gives Ibrahim's prayer for the valley, in Surah Ibrahim.
the empty valley in the story is where Mecca now stands
Ibrahim's prayer places it near the sacred House.
Hajar stopped asking questions and just accepted it
she kept asking, then changed the question: did Allah command this?

games.q: you're Hajar. Ibrahim is walking away, leaving you and the baby in an empty valley. he won't answer you. what do you ask?
o: how could you leave us here?
did Allah command you to do this?
games.why: she asks if Allah commanded it. he says yes, and she says He will not let us be lost, and goes back to the baby.

practice: Find the thing on your mind that you keep checking on, a test result, a child far away, money, a decision someone else is making, and hold it for a moment.

Then, on a long breath out, set it down, the way Hajar walked back to the baby; it won't stop being real, you're just not carrying it alone for these two minutes. If you pray, you can hand it over by name.

wordCard.voice: Hajar, left alone in the valley with a baby and a bag of dates, who found one question to stand on: did God command this?

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 14:37: "in a valley without crops," Ibrahim's words for the place he left them.

carryVoice: Your line: then we will not be lost. She walked back to the baby with that. Day thirty-nine.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3364 (Hajar and Isma'il left in the valley, narrated from Ibn Abbas)
Genesis 16 and 21 (Hagar, named as a neighbor)
